paragraphs.text: translated by
1. Ho there, my consort! Stay, thou fierce-souled lady, and let us reason for a while together.
paragraphs.original: हये जाये मनसा तिष्ठ घोरे वचांसि मिश्रा कृणवावहै नु ।
paragraphs.translit: haye jāye manasā tiṣṭha ghore vacāṃsi miśrā kṛṇavāvahai nu |

paragraphs.text: Such thoughts as these of ours, while yet unspoken in days gone by have never brought us comfort.
paragraphs.original: न नौ मन्त्रा अनुदितास एते मयस्करन्परतरे चनाहन्
paragraphs.translit: na nau mantrā anuditāsa ete mayaskaranparatare canāhan

paragraphs.text: 2. What am I now to do with this thy saying? I have gone from thee like the first of Mornings.
paragraphs.original: किमेता वाचा कृणवा तवाहं प्राक्रमिषमुषसामग्रियेव ।
paragraphs.translit: kimetā vācā kṛṇavā tavāhaṃ prākramiṣamuṣasāmagriyeva |

paragraphs.text: Pururavas, return thou to thy dwelling: I, like the wind, am difficult to capture.
paragraphs.original: पुरूरवः पुनरस्तं परेहि दुरापना वात इवाहमस्मि
paragraphs.translit: purūravaḥ punarastaṃ parehi durāpanā vāta ivāhamasmi

paragraphs.text: 3. Like a shaft sent for glory from the quiver, or swift-steed winning cattle winning hundreds.
paragraphs.original: इषुर्न श्रिय इषुधेरसना गोषाः शतसा न रंहिः ।
paragraphs.translit: iṣurna śriya iṣudherasanā goṣāḥ śatasā na raṃhiḥ |

paragraphs.text: The lightning seemed to flash, as cowards planned it. The minstrels bleated like a lamb in trouble.
paragraphs.original: अवीरे क्रतौ वि दविद्युतन्नोरा न मायुं चितयन्त धुनयः
paragraphs.translit: avīre kratau vi davidyutannorā na māyuṃ citayanta dhunayaḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. Giving her husband's father life and riches, from the near dwelling, when her lover craved her,
paragraphs.original: सा वसु दधती श्वशुराय वय उषो यदि वष्ट्यन्तिगृहात् ।
paragraphs.translit: sā vasu dadhatī śvaśurāya vaya uṣo yadi vaṣṭyantigṛhāt |

paragraphs.text: She sought the home wherein she found her pleasure, accepting day and night her lord's embraces.
paragraphs.original: अस्तं ननक्षे यस्मिञ्चाकन्दिवा नक्तं श्नथिता वैतसेन
paragraphs.translit: astaṃ nanakṣe yasmiñcākandivā naktaṃ śnathitā vaitasena

paragraphs.text: 5. Thrice in the day didst thou embrace thy consort, though coldly she received thy fond caresses.
paragraphs.original: त्रिः स्म माह्नः श्नथयो वैतसेनोत स्म मेऽव्यत्यै पृणासि ।
paragraphs.translit: triḥ sma māhnaḥ śnathayo vaitasenota sma me'vyatyai pṛṇāsi |

paragraphs.text: To thy desires, Pururavas, I yielded: so wast thou king, O hero, of my body.
paragraphs.original: पुरूरवोऽनु ते केतमायं राजा मे वीर तन्वस्तदासीः
paragraphs.translit: purūravo'nu te ketamāyaṃ rājā me vīra tanvastadāsīḥ

paragraphs.text: 6. The maids Sujirni, Sreni, Sumne-api, Charanyu, Granthini, and Hradecaksus,-
paragraphs.original: या सुजूर्णिः श्रेणिः सुम्नआपिर्ह्रदेचक्षुर्न ग्रन्थिनी चरण्युः ।
paragraphs.translit: yā sujūrṇiḥ śreṇiḥ sumnaāpirhradecakṣurna granthinī caraṇyuḥ |

paragraphs.text: These like red kine have hastened forth, the bright ones, and like milch-cows have lowed in emulation.
paragraphs.original: ता अञ्जयोऽरुणयो न सस्रुः श्रिये गावो न धेनवोऽनवन्त
paragraphs.translit: tā añjayo'ruṇayo na sasruḥ śriye gāvo na dhenavo'navanta

paragraphs.text: 7. While he was born the Dames sate down together, the Rivers with free kindness gave him nurture;
paragraphs.original: समस्मिञ्जायमान आसत ग्ना उतेमवर्धन्नद्यः स्वगूर्ताः ।
paragraphs.translit: samasmiñjāyamāna āsata gnā utemavardhannadyaḥ svagūrtāḥ |

paragraphs.text: And then, Pururavas, the Gods increased thee for mighty battle, to destroy the Dasyus.
paragraphs.original: महे यत्त्वा पुरूरवो रणायावर्धयन्दस्युहत्याय देवाः
paragraphs.translit: mahe yattvā purūravo raṇāyāvardhayandasyuhatyāya devāḥ

paragraphs.text: 8. When I, a mortal, wooed to mine embraces these heavenly nymphs who laid aside their raiment,
paragraphs.original: सचा यदासु जहतीष्वत्कममानुषीषु मानुषो निषेवे ।
paragraphs.translit: sacā yadāsu jahatīṣvatkamamānuṣīṣu mānuṣo niṣeve |

paragraphs.text: Like a scared snake they fled from me in terror, like chariot horses when the car has touched them.
paragraphs.original: अप स्म मत्तरसन्ती न भुज्युस्ता अत्रसन्रथस्पृशो नाश्वाः
paragraphs.translit: apa sma mattarasantī na bhujyustā atrasanrathaspṛśo nāśvāḥ

paragraphs.text: 9. When, loving these Immortal Ones, the mortal hath converse with the nymphs as they allow him.
paragraphs.original: यदासु मर्तो अमृतासु निस्पृक्सं क्षोणीभिः क्रतुभिर्न पृङ्क्ते ।
paragraphs.translit: yadāsu marto amṛtāsu nispṛksaṃ kṣoṇībhiḥ kratubhirna pṛṅkte |

paragraphs.text: Like swans they show the beauty of their bodies, like horses in their play they bite and nibble.
paragraphs.original: ता आतयो न तन्वः शुम्भत स्वा अश्वासो न क्रीळयो दन्दशानाः
paragraphs.translit: tā ātayo na tanvaḥ śumbhata svā aśvāso na krīḷayo dandaśānāḥ

paragraphs.text: 10. She who flashed brilliant as the falling lightning brought me delicious presents from the waters.
paragraphs.original: विद्युन्न या पतन्ती दविद्योद्भरन्ती मे अप्या काम्यानि ।
paragraphs.translit: vidyunna yā patantī davidyodbharantī me apyā kāmyāni |

paragraphs.text: Now from the flood be born a strong young hero May Uruvasi prolong her life for ever
paragraphs.original: जनिष्टो अपो नर्यः सुजातः प्रोर्वशी तिरत दीर्घमायुः
paragraphs.translit: janiṣṭo apo naryaḥ sujātaḥ prorvaśī tirata dīrghamāyuḥ

paragraphs.text: 11. Thy birth hath made me drink from earthly milch-kine: this power, Pururavas, hast thou vouchsafed me.
paragraphs.original: जज्ञिष इत्था गोपीथ्याय हि दधाथ तत्पुरूरवो म ओजः ।
paragraphs.translit: jajñiṣa itthā gopīthyāya hi dadhātha tatpurūravo ma ojaḥ |

paragraphs.text: I knew, and, warned thee, on that day. Thou wouldst not hear me. What sayest thou, when naught avails thee?
paragraphs.original: अशासं त्वा विदुषी सस्मिन्नहन्न म आशृणोः किमभुग्वदासि
paragraphs.translit: aśāsaṃ tvā viduṣī sasminnahanna ma āśṛṇoḥ kimabhugvadāsi

paragraphs.text: 12. When will the son be born and seek his father? Mourner-like, will he weep when first he knows him?
paragraphs.original: कदा सूनुः पितरं जात इच्छाच्चक्रन्नाश्रु वर्तयद्विजानन् ।
paragraphs.translit: kadā sūnuḥ pitaraṃ jāta icchāccakrannāśru vartayadvijānan |

paragraphs.text: Who shall divide the accordant wife and husband, while fire is shining with thy consort's parents?
paragraphs.original: को दम्पती समनसा वि यूयोदध यदग्निः श्वशुरेषु दीदयत्
paragraphs.translit: ko dampatī samanasā vi yūyodadha yadagniḥ śvaśureṣu dīdayat

paragraphs.text: 13. I will console him when his tears are falling: he shall not weep and cry for care that blesses.
paragraphs.original: प्रति ब्रवाणि वर्तयते अश्रु चक्रन्न क्रन्ददाध्ये शिवायै ।
paragraphs.translit: prati bravāṇi vartayate aśru cakranna krandadādhye śivāyai |

paragraphs.text: That which is thine, between us, will I send thee. Go home again, thou fool; thou hast not won me.
paragraphs.original: प्र तत्ते हिनवा यत्ते अस्मे परेह्यस्तं नहि मूर मापः
paragraphs.translit: pra tatte hinavā yatte asme parehyastaṃ nahi mūra māpaḥ

paragraphs.text: 14. Thy lover shall flee forth this day for ever, to seek, without return, the farthest distance.
paragraphs.original: सुदेवो अद्य प्रपतेदनावृत्परावतं परमां गन्तवा उ ।
paragraphs.translit: sudevo adya prapatedanāvṛtparāvataṃ paramāṃ gantavā u |

paragraphs.text: Then let his bed be in Destruction's bosom, and there let fierce rapacious wolves devour him.
paragraphs.original: अधा शयीत निरृतेरुपस्थेऽधैनं वृका रभसासो अद्युः
paragraphs.translit: adhā śayīta nirṛterupasthe'dhainaṃ vṛkā rabhasāso adyuḥ

paragraphs.text: 15. Nay, do not die, Pururavas, nor vanish: let not the evil-omened wolves devour thee.
paragraphs.original: पुरूरवो मा मृथा मा प्र पप्तो मा त्वा वृकासो अशिवास उ क्षन् ।
paragraphs.translit: purūravo mā mṛthā mā pra papto mā tvā vṛkāso aśivāsa u kṣan |

paragraphs.text: With women there can be no lasting friendship: hearts of hyenas are the hearts of women.
paragraphs.original: न वै स्त्रैणानि सख्यानि सन्ति सालावृकाणां हृदयान्येता
paragraphs.translit: na vai straiṇāni sakhyāni santi sālāvṛkāṇāṃ hṛdayānyetā

paragraphs.text: 16. When amid men in altered shape I sojourned, and through four autumns spent the nights among them,
paragraphs.original: यद्विरूपाचरं मर्त्येष्ववसं रात्रीः शरदश्चतस्रः ।
paragraphs.translit: yadvirūpācaraṃ martyeṣvavasaṃ rātrīḥ śaradaścatasraḥ |

paragraphs.text: I tasted once a day a drop of butter; and even now with that am I am contented.
paragraphs.original: घृतस्य स्तोकं सकृदह्न आश्नां तादेवेदं तातृपाणा चरामि
paragraphs.translit: ghṛtasya stokaṃ sakṛdahna āśnāṃ tādevedaṃ tātṛpāṇā carāmi

paragraphs.text: 17. I, her best love, call Urvasi to meet me, her who fills air and measures out the region.
paragraphs.original: अन्तरिक्षप्रां रजसो विमानीमुप शिक्षाम्युर्वशीं वसिष्ठः ।
paragraphs.translit: antarikṣaprāṃ rajaso vimānīmupa śikṣāmyurvaśīṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Let the gift brought by piety approach thee. Turn thou to me again: my heart is troubled.
paragraphs.original: उप त्वा रातिः सुकृतस्य तिष्ठान्नि वर्तस्व हृदयं तप्यते मे
paragraphs.translit: upa tvā rātiḥ sukṛtasya tiṣṭhānni vartasva hṛdayaṃ tapyate me

paragraphs.text: 18. Thus speak these Gods to thee, O son of Ila: As death hath verily got thee for his subject,
paragraphs.original: इति त्वा देवा इम आहुरैळ यथेमेतद्भवसि मृत्युबन्धुः ।
paragraphs.translit: iti tvā devā ima āhuraiḷa yathemetadbhavasi mṛtyubandhuḥ |

paragraphs.text: Thy sons shall serve the Gods with their oblation, and thou, moreover, shalt rejoice in Svarga.
paragraphs.original: प्रजा ते देवान्हविषा यजाति स्वर्ग उ त्वमपि मादयासे
paragraphs.translit: prajā te devānhaviṣā yajāti svarga u tvamapi mādayāse
